page.layout: Running head at top, with the page number at top left. Two engraved coin medallions side by side at the top (illustrations, with legends around their rims). Below them one column of running text with two entries, each a paragraph. No notes in the margins, no footnotes.

main_text.l: ALCIBIADES Atheniensium Dux, ad bellum Si-
culum missus est anno mundi 3548. ante Christum natum
414.hic erat aetatis flore, formae venera tione, nec minus elo-
quentia insignis:sed in conciliandis amicitiarum studiis quàm
in retinendis vir melior. Siculi itaque belli concitator & Dux
Alcibiades, Athenis infimulatur:reuocatus à bello ad iudi-
cium, siue conscientiam, siue indignitatem rei non ferens, ta-
citus in exilium Elidem proficiscitur:deinde Lacedaemona se
confert.Lacedaemoniorum Regem aduersus Atheniensis im-
pellit: sed huius virtus plus inuidiae quàm gratiae apud Lace-
daemonios contraxit: quare praemonitus à Tinaea vxore Regis,
quam adulterio cognouerat,sibi tendi insidias, ad Tisafernem
Darij praefectum profugit. Circa haec tempora Atheniensis
Lacedaemonios vicerunt ad Arginusas.Alcibiades ad Chalce-
donem victoria est potitus: Byzantium per proditionem obti-
nuit : Lacedaemonios vicit,Pharnabazum fudit.Vide Xenoph.
li.2.de reb.Graec.Tandem Atheniensium iussu vulneribus mul-
tis confossus occubuit. Iustin.lib.5.Plut.in Alci.Thuci.li.6. hic
in Lacedaemoniorum gratiam à Pharnabazi militibus occisus
dicitur: alij à quibusdam familiaribus,quando cum eorum
sorore congressum haberet.
TIMANDRA meretrix fuit quam deperibat Alcibia-
des, cui haec Timandra funus satis amplum atque magnifi-
cum pro suis facultatibus curauit faciendum. huius Timan-
drae filiam fuisse dicunt Laidem, quam Corynthiam appella-
bant: Sic matrem sequitur sua proles. Vide Plutarchum in
Alcibiade.

page.notes: Two engraved coin medallions at the top, with legends around the rims. Left coin: a male profile head, legend in Greek capitals (partly readable as ΑΛΚΙΒΙ... and ΑΘΗΝ...), not transcribed. Right coin: a female profile head with a diadem, legend reading TIMANDRA at left and M. CORIN. at right. The coin legends are part of the engraving and are not transcribed as text. The page number "110" is printed in a small decorative style at top left and was read as 110.
